workflows.name: Raster plan and site survey to registered IFC
workflows.output_scope: IFC4 project with site/building/storey hierarchy, explicit IfcWall and IfcOpeningElement records, a scan-to-building registration transform, IFC-derived mesh, and optional Blender/GLB inspection derivative.
workflows.comparison_conditions: Full route assumes a correctly scaled plan, a modest static site, overlapped photos, calibrated depth frames, and surveyed controls in shared frames. IFC-only from a clean vector plan skips SfM/MVS and scan registration. The image/mesh route supplies appearance/surface evidence; it does not create valid building semantics without authored classifications.

inputs.minimum_quality: Named project, building use and intended elements; ambiguities recorded.
inputs.handling: Normalize into model-brief; preserve wording and revisions.

inputs.minimum_quality: Readable plan view with known scale or surveyed control lengths, north/orientation and floor datum.
inputs.handling: Do not scale from page display size.

inputs.minimum_quality: Units and datum beside each value; dimensions can be traced to plan pixels or survey.
inputs.handling: Input to geometry; no silent defaults.

inputs.minimum_quality: Static scene with overlap, sharp exposure and sufficient texture; camera/lens metadata retained.
inputs.handling: Frames can be sampled from video but retain original frame mapping.

inputs.minimum_quality: Depth scale, intrinsics, sensor-to-rig extrinsics, invalid-depth mask and capture pose/time.
inputs.handling: Preserve raw depth frames.

inputs.minimum_quality: Independent control point coordinates and lengths in named frames, with uncertainty/status.
inputs.handling: Separate registration controls and held-out checks.

inputs.minimum_quality: Exact asset file/revision and item-level terms.
inputs.handling: Do not treat catalog access as a blanket content licence.

reference_points.frame: Project-local engineering frame; X east, Y north, Z up only when explicitly selected.
project plan frame and wall-local frame

reference_points.source_status: survey/CRS authority; never inferred from image appearance

checks: IFC schema parse and expected IFC4 file header.
Project length/area/volume units equal declared inputs.
Every wall has a unique GlobalId and storey containment; each opening has a unique GlobalId and expected representation.
`IfcRelVoidsElement` connects each opening to exactly its host wall; opening/wall local transforms agree.
Bonsai/IfcConvert independent reopen; compare bounds, volume, orientation and IDs.
Registration controls vs held-out control residuals, in local regions and units.
COLMAP camera reprojection and depth/photogrammetry overlap; metric scale only with source controls.
failure_recovery: Plan scale or north conflict: keep input unchanged; fix the calibration record, regenerate a new IFC path and compare reports.
Missing openings or invalid IFC feature relation: inspect per-wall opening dimensions and rerun against new target, not the old file.
COLMAP disconnected camera clusters: separate reconstruction components, add overlap images or supply known camera poses; do not merge by visual guess.
ICP drift: return to survey control correspondences and global registration; do not accept local RMSE alone.
Low memory: reduce image resolution/patch source count or omit MVS; keep the sparse camera solve and label result as surface-incomplete.

effort.human_reason: Plan interpretation, element classification, multi-source registration and georeferencing require expert decisions. IFC-only from an already vectorized/dimensioned plan is substantially easier.
effort.setup_reason: Combines IFC authoring, camera solve/MVS, point-cloud registration, model licensing and geometry/display adapters.
effort.compute_reason: Sparse reconstruction and IFC creation are CPU/modest; dense multi-view stereo, multiple image batches and large point clouds dominate. DOM contract rates the complete plan+survey+registered IFC path.

resources.cpu: CPU for API/IFC parsing and controls; multithreading for geometry/reconstruction.
resources.gpu: COLMAP dense PatchMatch benefits from CUDA-capable GPU; CPU-only feature/matching path exists; depth registration can remain CPU.
resources.ram: IFC graph size, raster dimensions, number of cameras, dense depth maps and point count drive RAM.
resources.storage: Original images/depth frames, SfM database, dense depth maps, clouds, IFC and display derivatives; preserve separate source and output trees.
scaling_drivers: mesh/cloud points and IFC element count
stored copies of intermediate depth maps
variants: Vectorized plan and no survey MVS lower effort and compute.
Photos without control points yield reconstruction with arbitrary scale.
Depth frames calibrated to survey frame reduce SfM workload.
BIM semantics remain human-authored even with high-quality surfaces.

workflows.name: Manufacturer STEP component to robot link
workflows.output_scope: One sourced supplier component imported as CAD solid; explicit component record, robot parent/link role and reviewed joint; separate visual and collision mesh; sourced mass/inertial fields; URDF link package. An MJCF source/alternative is produced by the local reference writer, not by the URDF export stage.
workflows.comparison_conditions: Comparison condition: one small-to-medium supplier STEP solid, source revision and rights located, mounting datums measured, target parent frame/joint intent stated, mass and inertia sourced or calculated from volume+density with assumptions. Multi-part gearboxes, closed kinematic loops and uncertain vendor data increase human effort. The output is a robot-description link, not physical qualification.

checks: STEP file revision/hash and units.
CAD import bounds, mass/volume and mounting dimensions against vendor drawing/measurement.
Joint graph tree and axis/origin/limit source.
URDF parses; every relative mesh path resolves; joint transforms match FreeCAD assembly.
Inertial values are sourced, framed and pass numerical tensor checks.
Visual and collision files are separate and generated from the same source revision.
Asset redistribution terms are attached to file; packaging does not silently relicense vendor geometry.
failure_recovery: STEP importer fails or units wrong: keep original, inspect AP schema/units and import in independent kernel before conversion.
No usable mass/inertia: preserve unknown fields as unknown; do not use arbitrary geometry density.
Mounting axis ambiguous: request measured datum or author an explicit design datum; do not fit it visually.
URDF importer rejects joint type or loop: use a documented tree adapter or native MJCF with explicit constraint topology.
Collision creates false contact: go back to visual CAD; split per-link collision bodies or choose primitives using contact needs.

effort.human_reason: A single supplier part is quick to import, but choosing its parent, motion, interfaces, tolerance, mass and license requires human evidence.
effort.setup_reason: CAD import, rights registry, mesh/collider tool and URDF adapter are separate.
effort.compute_reason: For one part, mesh export, URDF parsing and mass data are small; large assemblies are outside the comparison condition.
